rules.title: extern ABI string whitelist
rules.statement: The ABI string of an `extern "ABI" { … }` block or an `extern "ABI" fn …` item must be one of "C", "C-unwind", "system", or "Rust" (enclosing quotes optional); any other string is rejected.
rules.divergence: A7: "C-unwind" is accepted at parse but unwinding-across-FFI is moot (panic=abort).

rules.title: extern block flattening and ABI inheritance
rules.statement: An `extern "ABI" { extern_fn* }` block flattens to a linear item worklist; each child extern-fn that does not carry its own ABI inherits the block's ABI string, and item collection treats grouped and flat extern fns identically.

rules.title: union shares struct collection shape
rules.statement: A `union NAME { … }` is collected with the same named-field/type-param shape as a struct and registered as a known type, with its `is_union` flag set.
examples: union U { i: i32, f: f32 }

rules.title: fieldless union rejected
rules.statement: A union with zero fields is rejected; a union must declare at least one field.

rules.title: union field types restricted to non-move types
rules.statement: Each non-generic union field type must not be a move type (Vec/Box/String/owning trait object); allowed are Copy types, references, ManuallyDrop<T>, or aggregates thereof. A field whose type is a bare type-parameter is exempt at collection (checked at monomorphization); a field that is itself a union is allowed.
rules.uncertainty: Slice-1 uses is_move_type as the rejection oracle; full ManuallyDrop/tuple/array recursion is a follow-up.
rules.divergence: B: generic-union Copy check is deferred to mono rather than enforced at use site as in Rust.

rules.title: #[repr(transparent)] requires single field
rules.statement: `#[repr(transparent)]` on a struct sets repr_transparent (the wrapper inherits its single field's layout) and requires the struct to have exactly one field, else it is rejected.

rules.title: non-transparent struct repr modes rejected
rules.statement: On a struct, `#[repr]` with no argument is an error, and any repr mode other than `transparent` (e.g. `C`, `packed`, `align(...)`) is parse-then-reject (not silently accepted).

rules.title: structural struct attribute flags
rules.statement: Recognised structural struct attributes set per-struct flags: no_auto_drop, self_describing, rel_ptr, pinned, zone_mut, zoned (zoned2), borrow_carrying, non_null.

rules.title: exclusive datatype annotations are unique
rules.statement: On a datatype, the exclusive annotations `#[type_code]` and `#[annotation]` may each appear at most once; a duplicate occurrence is rejected.

rules.title: #[type_code=N] registers explicit type code
rules.statement: `#[type_code=N]` on a datatype registers N as the explicit type code for the datatype's fully-qualified name, making it resolvable by impl-collection in the same pass; `#[annotation]` flags the datatype as a user-annotation type.

rules.title: #[repr(uN/iN)] sets enum discriminant width
rules.statement: `#[repr(I)]` on an enum where I is an integer type (u8/u16/u32/u64/i8/i16/i32/i64/usize/isize) sets the enum's backing (discriminant) type; it conflicts with (errors against) an already-declared `enum Foo : I'` backing type when I≠I'. `#[repr(C)]` and other non-integer modes are parse-then-reject.

rules.title: #[zoned]/#[borrow_carrying] on enum
rules.statement: `#[zoned]` on an enum sets its zoned2 flag (niche-enum Ref arm stored self-relative at rest, absolute as value); `#[borrow_carrying]` sets the borrow_carrying flag.

rules.title: #[no_mangle] keeps bare symbol name
rules.statement: `#[no_mangle]` on a function causes the bare base name to be used as the symbol name (no name mangling).

rules.title: test-harness function attributes
rules.statement: `#[test]`, `#[ignore]`, and `#[should_panic]` are recognised on a function; `#[should_panic(expected = "…")]` records the expected panic substring from its string-literal argument.

rules.title: #[metaprog_handler("trigger")] registers a hook
rules.statement: `#[metaprog_handler("trigger")]` on a function registers (trigger, fn-name); the trigger is the first positional string-literal argument and the host driver invokes the hook on each user item carrying a matching `#[trigger]`.

rules.title: static link symbol qualification
rules.statement: A `static` with a value is registered with a module-qualified link symbol `<module_id>.<pkg>$<name>` (bare `<pkg>$<name>` when module_id empty) so two modules declaring the same `pkg::NAME` do not collide; an extern static (no value) links against the bare name.

rules.title: static mut and extern static require unsafe
rules.statement: A `static mut` is recorded as a mutable static (its reads/writes require `unsafe`); an extern static (declared with no value) is recorded as an extern static, every access of which requires `unsafe`.

rules.title: cfg-disabled items are dropped
rules.statement: Before collecting an item, `cfg_attr` activations are applied and `cfg(...)` predicates evaluated against pending annotations; if any predicate is false the item is dropped entirely (neither collected nor lowered) together with its pending annotations.

rules.title: doc comment accumulation and prefix stripping
rules.statement: `///` line docs strip the leading `///` plus one optional space; `/** */` outer block docs and `/*! */`/`//!` inner docs accumulate; outer docs attach to the next non-doc item, inner docs accumulate into a per-module inner-doc buffer joined by newlines and never attach to a specific item.

rules.title: enum backing type must be integer
rules.statement: An explicit enum backing type `enum Foo : T { … }` must be an integer kind; a non-integer T is rejected.

rules.title: empty enum body is legal
rules.statement: An enum with an empty body is legal (an uninhabited / marker type); no diagnostic is emitted.

rules.title: implicit enum discriminant sequencing
rules.statement: An enum variant without an explicit discriminant takes the value 0 for the first such variant and previous+1 thereafter; an explicit value resets the running counter to value+1.

rules.title: enum discriminant must fit backing type
rules.statement: When an enum has a backing type, each variant's discriminant value must fit in that backing integer type, else it is rejected.

rules.title: enum discriminant from const expression
rules.statement: An enum discriminant may be given by a general const expression (e.g. `1 << 1`), evaluated via CTFE; a `metacall { <expr> }` discriminant must contain a single integer tail expression, evaluated via CTFE to the discriminant value.
rules.divergence: A1: const-eval at discriminant position is via metacall/CTFE rather than miri.

rules.title: enum discriminant referencing another enum's variant
rules.statement: An enum discriminant may be `OtherEnum::OtherVariant` (with optional `as T` cast dropped): the referent is resolved among already-collected enums and its discriminant value is used verbatim; an unknown enum or variant is rejected.

rules.title: enum variant payload shapes
rules.statement: Enum variant payloads may be tuple-style (positional types), struct-shape (named fields, in declaration order, names must be unique), or variadic (single type ref); payload type positions are item signatures in which `_` is rejected (E0121).
examples: enum E { Tup(i32, i32), Rec { x: i32 }, Var(i32) }
